column4: According to Weiser, M. (2014), at about 3pm local time, Shasta-Trinity NF rangers reported a debris flow on south side of mountain in Mud Creek. Within 3 hours Pilgrim Creek Rd. and Forest Service Rd 31 buried. Mud continued coursing down overnight into Lake McCloud and McCloud River. Rangers think cause is Konwakiton Glacier near summit and may have released stored volume of water and eventually caused glacier dam to break. Event of this magnitude hasn't occurred at Shasta in 20yrs.

Volume estimates from de la Fuente and others (2016) from lidar differencing estimate 1 million cubic yards were eroded from Mud Creek watershed, 800,000 cubic yards were deposited on the fan above Highway 89. Uncertainties of about 2% for erosion are estimated. Values used in the database are those based on erosion. de la Fuente and others (2016) notes that the difference in eroded and deposited material could stem from an unknown amount of snow and ice that may have been incorporated in the estimates.

Seth Moran (written communication)"It looks like there is a signal that was picked up by basically all Shasta stations starting at 2100 UTC (2pm PDT), ~1 hour before the 3pm observation of the debris flow reported by USFS observers. There are a number of pulses between 2100-2230, with a fairly continuous signal recorded on station LMC (which looks to be located closest to the main drainage down which these flows came) for over 2 hours. There also are some smaller signals in the 30-40 minutes prior to 2100 that might be related, but harder to say."

de la Fuente and others (2016) summarizes what is known about this event and includes photos, eyewitness reports, lidar differencing results, map of flow path. Reconnaissance suggests the event originated at Konwakiton Glacier, evidence showing water and/or debris exited from both lobes, flowing in down three channels. Most of the debris was picked up by channel bank collapses at lower elevations.

Raw waveforms from closest stations. Data was demeaned but no other processing was applied. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present.

High frequency (1-5 Hz) ground velocity waveforms for station response from closest stations with detections. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Waveforms are corrected for station response after removing the mean. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Clipped waveforms have not been removed before station correction so check raw plots before interpreting high amplitude signals.
Spectrograms of velocity waveforms corrected for station sensitivity from closest stations with detections. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present

Multitaper spectra (same units as Power Spectral Density) of velocity waveforms corrected for station sensitivity from closest stations with detections. Linear trend was removed and a taper was applied before generating spectra. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Since station response was not removed to avoid adding artifacts at low frequencies for short and intermediate period stations, the lower frequency amplitudes should be interpreted with care.
